hypotheses.title: Nicotinamide Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of nicotinamide extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect operates through improved cellular NAD+ availability supporting maintenance and repair processes.
hypotheses.rationale: Nicotinamide is a precursor of NAD+, a cofactor central to energy metabolism, DNA repair, and sirtuin activity. Sustaining NAD+ supply could slow age-related functional decline and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving nicotinamide will exhibit a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to nicotinamide-supplemented or control diets and follow them until natural death. Compare survival curves using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: 17-alpha-Estradiol Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of 17-alpha-estradiol shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect reflects harmful disruption of endocrine or metabolic homeostasis by the compound.
hypotheses.rationale: Estrogenic compounds can perturb hormone signaling, cell proliferation, and metabolic regulation. Chronic exposure to a noncanonical estrogen could impose physiological stress that accelerates aging processes.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving 17-alpha-estradiol will exhibit a statistically significant decrease in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to 17-alpha-estradiol-treated or control diets and follow them until natural death. Compare survival curves using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: 17-alpha-Estradiol Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of 17-alpha-estradiol extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect operates through modulation of metabolic and stress-resistance pathways without classical estrogen receptor activation.
hypotheses.rationale: 17-alpha-estradiol is a weak estrogen isomer that can influence inflammation, lipid metabolism, and oxidative stress responses. Such shifts in systemic physiology could slow aging and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving 17-alpha-estradiol will exhibit a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to 17-alpha-estradiol-treated or control diets and follow them until natural death. Compare survival curves using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Sodium Thiosulfate Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of sodium thiosulfate extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The effect operates through sulfide-based modulation of redox balance and mitochondrial function.
hypotheses.rationale: Thiosulfate serves as a sulfur donor supporting hydrogen sulfide signaling, which influences vascular function, antioxidant defenses, and mitochondrial activity. Enhanced sulfide signaling could slow age-related decline.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving sodium thiosulfate will exhibit a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to sodium thiosulfate-supplemented or control water and follow them until natural death. Compare survival curves using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.rationale: Lovaza provides concentrated omega-3 fatty acids that incorporate into membranes and generate anti-inflammatory lipid mediators. Reduced chronic inflammation and improved lipid handling could decelerate aging.

hypotheses.rationale: Coenzyme Q10 shuttles electrons in the mitochondrial respiratory chain and quenches lipid peroxidation in membranes. Preserved mitochondrial efficiency and reduced oxidative damage could slow aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving coenzyme Q10 will exhibit a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.

hypotheses.title: Lovaza Extends Lifespan via SIRT1 Activation
hypotheses.claim: Administration of Lovaza extends lifespan in Mus musculus by activating SIRT1 deacetylase pathways. The lifespan effect depends mechanistically on SIRT1-mediated regulation of metabolism and stress resistance.
hypotheses.rationale: Omega-3 fatty acids can influence NAD+-dependent sirtuin signaling, and SIRT1 deacetylates targets governing inflammation, mitochondrial biogenesis, and stress responses. SIRT1 activation could therefore mediate lifespan extension.
hypotheses.prediction: Lovaza-treated mice will live significantly longer than controls, and this extension will be abolished in mice with SIRT1 loss of function.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat wild-type and SIRT1-knockout mice with Lovaza or control diets and follow all groups until natural death. Compare survival curves across genotype and treatment using log-rank analysis.
